paper.title: Oracle-Efficient Hybrid Online Learning with Unknown Distribution

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid online learning (i.i.d. unknown features, adaptive adversarial labels)
unmapped: features x_t drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution mu (no sampling access); labels y_t in [0,1] chosen adaptively by adversary
learner predicts y_hat in [0,1] and competes with the best hypothesis in a class H (online supervised learning with hypothesis class)
loss convex in first argument and L-Lipschitz in both arguments
access to an offline (mixed) ERM oracle for H
settings.definition_quote: Nature selects an (unknown) distribution $\mu$ over $\mathcal{X}$ at the start of the game. At each time step $t$, Nature independently samples $\x_t \sim \mu$ and selects \emph{adversarially} a $y_t \in [0,1]$, but reveals only $\x_t$. ... the loss $\ell$ is \emph{convex} in its first argument and $L$-Lipschitz in \emph{both} arguments

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid online learning with oblivious adversary
unmapped: features i.i.d. from unknown mu; adversary fixes label functions f_1..f_T in advance, y_t = f_t(x_t)
competes with best hypothesis in class H; ERM oracle access
settings.definition_quote: the adversary fixes functions $f_1,\cdots,f_T:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow [0,1]$ before the game and sets the adversary labels $y_t=f_t(\x_t)$ for each time step $t\in [T]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid online learning with shifting distributions (K changes)
unmapped: feature distribution piecewise i.i.d. with at most S_T (paper's K) arbitrary unknown change points and distributions; labels adaptive adversarial
binary-valued hypothesis class with finite VC dimension; ERM oracle access
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the total number of changes is upper bounded by $K$, while the selection of distributions and change points are completely arbitrary.

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid contextual K-armed bandits (unknown i.i.d. contexts, adversarial costs)
unmapped: context distribution unknown with no sampling access; costs c_t in [0,1]^K chosen adaptively
finite policy class H of size N_exp; ERM oracle access
regret measured with expected loss <q_t, c_t>
settings.definition_quote: Nature selects some $\mu$ at the start of the game. At each time step $t$, Nature samples $\x_t \sim \mu$ and selects \emph{adversarially} a cost vector $c_t \in [0,1]^K$, but reveals only $\x_t$. ... Nature reveals only $c_t[\hat{y}_t]$

algorithms.name: Epoch-based surrogate relaxation with random play-out from empirical distribution (Psi)
Fixed-length epoch restart of the oracle-efficient predictor (shifting distributions)
Epoch-based relaxation contextual bandit predictor (adapted from Syrgkanis et al. 2016 with hallucinated contexts from empirical distribution)

symbols.q: exponent such that Rad_T(H) <= O(T^q), q in [1/2,1]

conditions: loss convex in first argument and L-Lipschitz
tuning: epoch length M(n) = n^alpha with alpha = 1/(2(1-q))

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H} \subset [0,1]^{\mathcal{X}}$ be a class with $\mathsf{Rad}_T(\mathcal{H}) \le O(T^{q})$ for some $q \in [\frac{1}{2},1]$, and let $\ell$ be a $L$-Lipschitz loss that is convex in its first argument. Then there exists an \emph{oracle-efficient} prediction rule $\Phi$ with at most $O(L\sqrt{T}\log T)$ calls to the ERM oracle per round, such that \[\tilde{r}_T(\mathcal{H},\Phi) \le O\left(L\sqrt{\log (LT)} \cdot T^{\frac{2-q}{3-2q}}\right).\]

results.notes: Oracle-efficient (polynomial given ERM oracle). Epoch schedule does not depend on T, so marked anytime. Setting mapping of online supervised learning onto ontology is approximate.

symbols.VC: VC dimension of the binary-valued class H

conditions: H binary-valued with finite VC dimension

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: In particular, for a binary-valued class with finite VC-dimension, we have \(\tilde{r}_T(\mathcal{H},\Phi) \le O(L\sqrt{\mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{H})\log (LT)} \cdot T^{\frac{3}{4}}),\)

symbols.p_fat: exponent p such that the alpha-fat-shattering dimension of H is of order alpha^{-p}

conditions: H real-valued with alpha-fat shattering dimension of order alpha^{-p}, p > 0

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: and for a real-valued class $\mathcal{H}$ with an $\alpha$-fat shattering dimension of order $\alpha^{-p}$ for $p>0$~\citep{alon1997scale}, we have \(\tilde{r}_T(\mathcal{H},\Phi) \le \tilde{O}(L T^{\max\{\frac{3}{4},\frac{p+1}{p+2}\}}).\)

symbols.M_side: horizon M of the game with side information
symbols.N_side: number N of i.i.d. side-information samples from mu
symbols.Rad_M: Rademacher complexity of H at horizon M
symbols.c_const: unspecified absolute constant hidden in O(.)

conditions: hypothetical game: learner (and adversary) receive N i.i.d. side samples from mu before a game of length M

source.label: thm:main2
source.quote: Let $\Phi$ be the predictor as in (\ref{eq:predictor}) and $M\le N/2$. Then for any class $\mathcal{H}\subset [0,1]^{\mathcal{X}}$ with a convex and $L$-Lipschitz loss $\ell$, the predictor $\Phi$ can be computed efficiently with access to at most $O(L\sqrt{M}\log M)$ mixed-ERM oracle calls per round such that \tilde{r}_{M,N}^{\mathsf{side}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le 2L\mathsf{Rad}_M(\mathcal{H})+\sqrt{M}+O(...)

results.notes: Intermediate side-information result; horizon M is the game length; mixed exact/O expression, recorded as exact with an explicit unspecified constant.

symbols.VC_u: VC dimension of the class of pointwise suprema of subsets of H
symbols.VC_i: VC dimension of the class of pointwise infima of subsets of H

source.label: cor1
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}\subset \{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{u}}=\{f_{\mathcal{H}'}(\x)=\sup_{h\in \mathcal{H}'}\{h(\x)\}:\mathcal{H}'\subset \mathcal{H}\}$, $\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{i}}=...$ be two classes of functions and $\ell$ be the absolute loss. Then there exists an oracle-efficient predictor $\Phi$ satisfying $\tilde{r}_T(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le O(\sqrt{\max\{\mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{u}}), \mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{i}})\}T})$.

conditions: H = all 1-Lipschitz functions [0,1]^d -> [0,1] under L_inf norm

source.label: th-lipschitz
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}$ and $\ell$ be as above. Then, there exists an oracle-efficient predictor $\Phi$ such that $\tilde{r}_{T}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le \tilde{O}(T^{\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{d-1}{d}\}})$, and this bound is tight upto poly-logarithmic factors.

source.label: th-lipschitz
source.quote: and this bound is tight upto poly-logarithmic factors.

results.notes: Lower bound only asserted via metric entropy Theta(eps^{-d}) argument, no explicit statement of form; recorded as Omega_tilde.

symbols.q: exponent such that Rad_T(H) = O(T^q), q in [1/2,1]

source.label: thm:obregret
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}\subset [0,1]^{\mathcal{X}}$ be a class of Rademacher complexity $\mathsf{Rad}_T(\mathcal{H})=O(T^q)$ for some $q\in [\frac{1}{2},1]$ and $\ell$ be the absolute loss. Then there exists an oracle-efficient prediction rule $\Phi$ with at most $O(\sqrt{T}\log T)$ calls to the ERM oracle per round, such that $\tilde{r}_{T}^{\mathsf{ob}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le O(T^q)$.

source.label: thm:obregret
source.quote: In particular, for finite-VC class $\mathcal{H}$, we have $\tilde{r}_{T}^{\mathsf{ob}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le O(\sqrt{\mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{H})T})$.

symbols.p_fat: exponent p such that the alpha-fat-shattering dimension of H is O(alpha^{-p})

source.label: thm:obregret
source.quote: For a class $\mathcal{H}$ with $\alpha$-fat shattering dimension $O(\alpha^{-p})$ for some $p>0$, we have $\tilde{r}_{T}^{\mathsf{ob}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le \tilde{O}(T^{\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{p-1}{p}\}})$.

conditions: H binary-valued with finite VC dimension
at most S_T (paper's K) distribution changes

source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}\subset \{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$ be a binary valued class with finite VC-dimension under a convex and $L$-Lipschitz loss. Then there exists an oracle-efficient predictor $\Phi$ such that if the features are generated by the process with change cost $K$ and the labels are generated adversarially, then the hybrid minimax regret as (\ref{eq:hbreg}) is upper bounded by $O\left(L\sqrt{\mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{H})\log(LT)}K^{\frac{1}{5}}T^{\frac{4}{5}}\right).$

results.notes: Paper's K = number of distribution changes, mapped to S_T. Tuning of B uses T and K.

conditions: finite policy class H with |H| = N_exp

source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}\subset [K]^{\mathcal{X}}$ be a finite policy set. Then there exists an oracle-efficient predictor $\Phi$ such that the hybrid bandit minimax regret defined in Section~\ref{sec:def} is upper bounded by $$\tilde{r}_T^{\mathsf{bandit}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le O\left((K^{\frac{2}{3}}(\log|\mathcal{H}|)^{\frac{1}{3}}+K\sqrt{\log K})\cdot T^{\frac{4}{5}}\right).$$

results.notes: Regret uses expected loss <q_t,c_t> against best policy; expectation over contexts and adaptive costs.
